items.actClause:
AN ACT to establish the passenger safety task force on safety for passengers
transported by stretch limousines
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6189

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to establish the passenger safety task force on
safety for passengers transported by stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To create a Passenger Safety Task Force to study issues related to safe-
ty for passengers transported by.stretch limousines.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill creates. the Passenger. Safety Task Force. The
task force will consist of twenty members, with the Commissioners of the
New York State Department of Motor Vehicles and the New York State
Department of Transportation serving as co-chairs. The additional eigh-
teen members will include representatives from each of the eleven
Department of Transportation regions, the superintendent of the New York
State Police, and six members appointed by the Governor, the Temporary
President of the Senate, and the Speaker of the Assembly.

The task force shall undertake a review of the actions and measures that
are needed to ensure safe, adequate, efficient and reliable passenger
transportation by stretch limousine. The task force Shall issue a final
report and make recommendations regarding: (a) the promotion of enhanced
coordination and uniformity between the New York State Department of
Motor Vehicles and the New York State Department of Transportation
regarding the regulation of stretch limousines; (b) the establishment
and adoption of a uniform safety training program for drivers; (c) the
appropriateness of extending federal regulations that currently apply to
busdrivers to stretch limousines; (d) ,establishing a limit on the maxi-
mum allowable time frame for stretch limousines to be permitted to oper-
ate on state roadways; (e) the need for additional safety measures,
including traffic safety measures such as prohibiting drivers from
making U-turns or the use of hands-free devices while operating ,a
stretch limousine, and mandating installation of safety features like
multiple antiintrusion bars, in side panels, carbon monoxide monitors,
rear view cam eras, having New York State owned and operated inspection
stations for stretch limousines and providing for random spot vehicle
inspections, providing appropriate signage for customers, and the feasi-
bility of a New York State crash testing program; and (f) increasing
minimum age for drivers to obtain a license to, operate stretch limou-
sines.

The task force is directed to convene at least one public forum and
issue its final report within six months of convening.

Section two provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Stretch limousines are the vehicle of choise for many happy occasions,
from family events, to birthdays, to weddings, to the annual ritual of
prom. But they also present unique challenges that implicate the safety
of drivers and passengers alike.

As with any area where multiple state agencies must collaborate, period-
ic review of inter-agency and external communication is critical to
ensure passenger safety. Additionally, the current, set of regulations
does not reflect the ever-changing array of safety features available to
other motor vehicles that may be practically deployed in a stretch
limousine. Finally, there are a number of questions that are specific to
stretch limousines, such as whether there is an upper limit that ought
to be established in terms of how long or for how many miles such a
vehicle ought to be allowed to operate on the state's roadways.

The need for this review was underscored by the tragic July 2015 limou-
sine crash in Cutchogue, New York that killed four people and injured
four others. It was further reinforced by the final report and recommen-
dations of the Suffolk County Supreme Court Special Grand Jury, which
was impaneled to investigate that Cutchogue crash and suggested a number
of improvements in passenger safety and regulation that ought to be made
at the state and county level. It has been prompted anew in the wake of
another, even deadlier crash in Schoharie, NY.

The legislation implements this recommendation from the Special Grand
Jury report by creating a task force of owners and operators of busi-
nesses that utilize stretch limousines throughout the different
geographic regions of the state, understanding that the particular
issues in New York City may not be those experienced in Buffalo or Syra-
cuse, to say nothing of suburban and rural communities. The task force
would be convened and co-chaired by the designee of the Commissioner of
the NYS Department of Transportation and the Commissioner of the NYS
Department of Motor Vehicles. Since law enforcement will be required to
enforce any changes, the State Police ought to be represented as well.

Finally, the Governor, Speaker of the Assembly, and President of the
Senate would select additional appointees including representatives from
community groups and those with deep knowledge and commitment to the
issues of traffic safety and reducing accidents and fatalities more
broadly.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:.

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
30 days after being signed into law.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6189B

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to establish the stretch limousine passenger safety task force;
and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To create a Passenger Safety Task Force to study issues related to safe-
ty for passengers transported by stretch limousines.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This legislation creates a Stretch Limousine Passenger Safety Task
Force. The task force consists of 21 members, with the Commissioners of
the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles and the New York State
Department of Transportation serving as co-chairs, along with represen-
tatives from the State Police, and various Legislative and Executive
recommendations. The Task Force requires a minimum number of appointees
with expertise in motor vehicle occupant protection, crash avoidance and
crash-worthiness, motor vehicle alteration and construction, commercial
motor vehicle driver training, traffic safety, consumer protection and
public health and safety representatives, as well as representation from
the stretch limousine industry.

The task force shall undertake a review of the actions and measures that
are needed to ensure safe, adequate, efficient and reliable passenger
transportation by stretch limousine. The task force shall make recommen-
dations regarding: (a) the promotion of enhanced coordination and
uniformity between the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
and the New York State Department of Transportation (DOT) regarding the
regulation of stretch limousines;

(b) the establishment and adoption of a uniform safety training program
for drivers; (c) the appropriateness of extending federal regulations
that currently apply to bus drivers to stretch limousines; (d) reviewing
areas of federal preemption and where states have oversight roles; (e)
establishing a limit on the maximum allowable time frame for stretch
limousines to be permitted to operate on state roadways; (f) the need
for additional safety measures, including studying increasing the mini-
mum age for drivers to obtain a license to operate stretch limousines
traffic safety measures, mandating installation of safety features like
multiple anti-intrusion bars in side panels, roll-over protection
devices, emergency exits, carbon monoxide monitors, rear view cameras,
providing appropropriate signage for customers, and the feasibility of a
New York State crash testing program.

The task force is directed to convene at least one public forum and
issue its final report by May 1, 2021.

Section two provides the effective date.

from family events, to birthdays, to weddings, to the annual ritual of

prom. But they also present unique challenges that implicate the safety

ic review of inter-agency and external communication is critical to

four others. It was further reinforced by the final report and recommen-
dations of the Suffolk County Supreme Court Special Grand Jury, which
was impaneled to investigate that Cutchogue crash and suggested a number

nesses that utilize stretch limousines throughout the different

cuse, to say nothing of suburban and rural communities. The task force

2019: Similar bill (S.6189-A) passed Senate without objection.

To be determined.

30 days after being signed into law.
